subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.9 QQBot: long markdown reply is split into N independent bubbles (one per chunk), not a single message

question: Should QQBot keep the current by-design multi-message split for long Markdown, or should OpenClaw merge safe-size chunks into one QQ message when the merged payload stays under the safe byte limit?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the issue now conflicts with a QQBot owner's stated design reason for splitting and an open proof-positive PR that changes the user-visible delivery policy.

options.title: Confirm designed split and close the cluster
options.body: Treat multi-message Markdown splitting as the intended QQBot behavior to avoid truncation, then close this issue and the competing merge PRs with that rationale and any needed docs note.

options.title: Land bounded safe-size merge
options.body: Accept PR 99032 or an equivalent send-boundary merge so chunks under the 3600-byte safe limit send as one QQ message while oversized output keeps the current split path.

options.title: Request one live overflow comparison
options.body: Ask for live QQ proof that covers both below-limit merge and over-limit split behavior before choosing between the current design and the candidate merge path.

recommendation.title: Confirm designed split and close the cluster
recommendation.body: Treat multi-message Markdown splitting as the intended QQBot behavior to avoid truncation, then close this issue and the competing merge PRs with that rationale and any needed docs note.

likelyOwner.reason: Sliverp is listed for QQ/Chinese channels, authored the current chunker work, and already stated the current behavior is by design on this issue.
